raw_case_text:
A 63-year-old dark-skinned male patient, hypertensive, reported the appearance of erythematous-brown, edematous and itchy plaques on the abdomen in the beginning of 2013, with inconclusive histopathology and immunohistochemistry. He remained under follow-up and presented to the outpatient dermatology clinic in February 2015 with an ulcerated tumor on the skin of the nose and worsening of the previous lesions. On clinical examination, he had brown and edematous plaques on the frontal region, associated with alopecia of the eyebrows and hairline, in addition to a deforming tumor on the nose (Figure 1). ENT assessment demonstrated an infiltrative lesion, with total obstruction of the right nostril and partial of the left nostril, with associated mucoid discharge. No lesions on the palate or jugal mucosa were seen. Slightly lichenified brown plaques were seen on the upper and lower limbs, predominantly on the trunk and ulcerated tumors on the upper limbs (Figure 2).
There was no lymphadenopathy. The suspicion was of paracoccidioidomycosis, leishmaniasis, syphilis, leprosy, sarcoidosis, mycosis fungoides, and lethal midline granuloma. Blood samples were collected, and microscopy, Montenegro's test, tuberculin test, bacilloscopy, serology for hepatitis, HIV and syphilis were all performed, and all were negative. Chest radiograph and abdomen ultrasound were unremarkable. New biopsies were taken, with unspecific findings. The patient's follow-up was then irregular, with long intervals between appointments, with worsening of the tumor on the nose. In July 2015 three new biopsies from different skin lesions were taken and the histopathology of the abdominal plaque revealed a dense atypical mononuclear infiltrate, involving the remaining follicular sheath and eccrine glands associated to psoriasiform hyperplasia of the epidermis and granulomatous reaction (Figure 3). Immunohistochemistry favored the diagnostic interpretation of non-Hodgkin epidermotropic and folliculotropic T-cell cutaneous lymphoma, CD4 and CD30 positive (Figures 4 and 5). The patient was seen by the hematology team and chemotherapy with gemcitabine and interferon, associated to phototherapy were scheduled.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 63-year-old hypertensive male presented in February 2015 with a deforming ulcerated nasal tumor, bilateral nasal obstruction, eyebrow/hairline alopecia, and progressive erythematous-brown plaques and ulcerated tumors over his trunk and extremities.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In early 2013, the patient developed pruritic, edematous erythematous-brown abdominal plaques with initially inconclusive biopsies. By February 2015, the lesions had progressed to involve the forehead, scalp hairline, eyebrows, trunk, and limbs, accompanied by a deforming ulcerated nasal mass causing complete right nostril and partial left nostril obstruction.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for pruritus, nasal obstruction, mucoid nasal discharge, and progressive cutaneous plaques and ulcerated tumors.

objective.physical_examination: Deforming ulcerated tumor on the nose with total right nostril and partial left nostril obstruction and mucoid discharge (sparing the palate and buccal mucosa); edematous brown plaques on the forehead with eyebrow and frontal hairline madarosis/alopecia; slightly lichenified brown plaques over the trunk and limbs; and ulcerated tumors on the upper extremities, with no palpable lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: Direct microscopy, Montenegro skin test, tuberculin test, slit-skin bacilloscopy, and serologies for HIV, viral hepatitis, and syphilis were all negative. Chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound were normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Repeat skin biopsy of an abdominal plaque in July 2015 demonstrated psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia and a dense atypical mononuclear infiltrate with epidermotropism, folliculotropism, syringotropism (eccrine gland involvement), and a granulomatous reaction; immunohistochemistry was positive for CD4 and CD30.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis, paracoccidioidomycosis, leprosy, syphilis, and sarcoidosis were ruled out by negative Montenegro test, bacilloscopy, serologies, and serial biopsies; histopathology and immunohistochemistry (CD4+, CD30+) confirmed primary cutaneous epidermotropic and folliculotropic CD30+ T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (mycosis fungoides with large-cell transformation/folliculotropism). The patient was referred to hematology and scheduled for systemic gemcitabine, interferon, and phototherapy.
